Class DevelopmentMode

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.context.env.DevelopmentMode
public final class DevelopmentMode extends Object
The development mode of a running application.

Development mode is switched on by a development launcher (for example the micronaut-dev module) that keeps the process alive across restarts of the application context and reloads application classes. Components that would otherwise terminate the JVM, such as the file watch restart listener or the startup failure handling of the Micronaut launcher, do not do so while development mode is active, because the launcher owns the process.

Development mode is not the same as the Environment.DEVELOPMENT environment. The environment is a configuration profile any run may activate; development mode is only active when a launcher sets the PROPERTY property to true, in any case.

Beans that only run in development mode, or only outside it, are annotated with DevelopmentActive or DevelopmentInactive.

  • Method Details

    • isEnabled

      public static boolean isEnabled(PropertyResolver propertyResolver)
      Whether development mode is active for the given property resolver.

      Given the environment, Environment.isDevelopmentMode() answers the same and is the entry point to use; this method serves a property resolver that is not an environment.

      Parameters:
      propertyResolver - The property resolver, typically the environment
      Returns:
      True if development mode is active
      See Also:
      • Environment.isDevelopmentMode()

    • isEnabledBySystemProperty

      public static boolean isEnabledBySystemProperty()
      Whether development mode is active according to the system properties.

      A launcher sets the system property before the application context exists, so components that run before the environment is available can consult it.

      Returns:
      True if the system property is set to true
